en: The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Adornment of Immeasurable Life Spoken by the Buddha,
Volume One. Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperial Censor, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Illuminating Teaching, Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard:

At one time the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain near the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of thirty-two thousand bhikṣus, all of whom were arhats endowed with great supernormal powers.
Their names were:
the Venerable Ājñātakauṇḍinya, the Venerable Aśvajit, the Venerable Maṣṭapada,
the Venerable Mahānāman, the Venerable Bhadrapāla, the Venerable Yaśoda, and the Venerable Vimala.
Venerable Subāhu, Venerable Pūrṇa-kāśyapa, Venerable Gavāmpati,
Venerable Uruvilvā-Kāśyapa, Venerable Nadī-Kāśyapa, Venerable Śāriputra,
Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Venerable Mahākātyāyana, and the Venerable...
Mahākauṣṭhila, the Venerable Kapphiṇa, the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita,
the Venerable Maitrāyaṇīputra, the Venerable Aniruddha, the Venerable Nanda, the Venerable Kaṅkin,
the Venerable Subhūti, the Venerable Revata, and the Venerable Khāṇu.
Rāvaṇī-gina, the Venerable Mahārāgī, the Venerable Parāyaṇī-gina,
the Venerable Bakule, the Venerable Ānanda, the Venerable Rāhula, the Venerable Svāgata,
and others such as these, totaling thirty-two thousand people.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in homage, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha possesses pure faculties, a perfect countenance, and a jewel-adorned buddha-field; such merits as these are unprecedented.
What is the vast and sublime conduct that is practiced?
And what is the conduct practiced by the Buddhas of the past and the future?
I pray that you will explain this for me.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Excellent, excellent!
For the benefit of all sentient beings, you have conceived a heart of compassion and are able to ask the Tathāgata about this subtle and profound meaning."
Listen attentively now!
Reflect upon it well!
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha shall now speak for you.
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"In the past, immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago, there appeared in the world a Buddha, a World-Honored One, named Dīpaṃkara Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
Prior to that Buddha Dīpaṃkara, there was another World-Honored One who appeared in the world, named Pradīpajyotirāja Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Arciṣmat Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, another Buddha appeared in the world, named Caṇḍāṅgarakṣa Tathāgata.
Again, prior to that Buddha, another Buddha appeared in the world, named Sumerukalpa Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Candramukha Tathāgata.
Again, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Vimalamukha Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Tathāgata Asaṅga.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Tathāgata Nāgendra.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Sūryavaktra Tathāgata.
Again, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Girisvararāja Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Sumeruśikhara Tathāgata.
Again, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Kanakagarbha Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Fire-Light Tathāgata.
Again, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Immovable Ground Tathāgata.
Furthermore, before that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Vaidūryaprabha Tathāgata.
Again, before that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Candrarāja Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Sūryaghoṣa Tathāgata.
Again, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Kusumavyūha Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, another Buddha appeared in the world, named Śrīkūṭa Tathāgata.
Again, prior to that Buddha, another Buddha appeared in the world, named Sāgarabuddhivikrīḍitābhijñārāja Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, another Buddha appeared in the world, named Śrīprabha Tathāgata.
Again, prior to that Buddha, another Buddha appeared in the world, named Mahāgandhahastiprabha Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, another Buddha appeared in the world named Sarvāmalaviraja Tathāgata.
Again, prior to that Buddha, another Buddha appeared in the world named Śūramgamaśikhara Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Ratnaprabhāsa Tathāgata.
Again, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Bahuguṇadhāraṇābhijña Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Overcoming the Light of the Sun and Moon Tathāgata.
Moreover, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Supreme Lapis Lazuli Light Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there appeared in the world a Buddha named Wisdom-Flower Opening the Mind-Activity Birth Tathāgata.
Again, prior to that Buddha, there appeared in the world a Buddha named Great Flower Forest Pervasive King Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Candraprabha Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Vigatāvidyāndhakāra Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Pearl and Coral Canopy Tathāgata.
Again, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Sovereign King of the Dharma of the Three Vehicles Tathāgata.
Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Siṃhasāgarakūṭeśvararāja Tathāgata.
Again, prior to that Buddha, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Brahmasvaraveśarāja Tathāgata.

Furthermore, prior to that Buddha, there appeared in the world a Buddha named Lokeśvararāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.

Within that assembly of Dharma, there was a bhikṣu named Dharmakāra, who was foremost in faith and understanding, foremost in clear recollection, foremost in practice, foremost in diligence, foremost in wisdom, and foremost in the Mahāyāna.
At that time, the bhikṣu left his own dwelling and approached the Buddha; he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet and stood to one side.
He then praised the Buddha in verse for the majesty and serenity of his countenance, and further made a vast vow, reciting:
“The Tathāgata’s subtle form is so majestic and dignified that there is none equal to it in all the worlds;
his immeasurable radiance illuminates the ten directions, causing the sun, the moon, and fire-jewels to all lose their luster.”
May I attain the pure voice of a Buddha, Whose Dharma-sound pervades boundless realms;
Proclaiming the gates of precepts, concentration, and diligence, Thoroughly penetrating the profound and subtle Dharma.
Wisdom vast and deep as the ocean, The inner mind pure and free from worldly toil,
Transcending the boundless gates to evil realms, Swiftly reaching the ultimate shore of Bodhi.
Just as the immeasurable Buddhas of the past, Whose majestic radiance universally illumined the realm of sentient beings,
Acted as great guides for those multitudes of living beings, Delivering them from old age and death to bring them peace and security;
Constantly practicing the six pāramitās of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, concentration, and wisdom,
may those sentient beings who have not yet crossed over be enabled to cross, and those already crossed be led to attain Buddhahood.
I offer worship with all my being to hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddhas,
World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, so that I may achieve the fruit of nirvāṇa.
Furthermore, there are the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, Constantly emitting light that illuminates all;
Their sublime adornments are peerless and beyond compare— May I achieve these so as to benefit all beings.

May all classes of sentient beings wandering through the various realms of existence within all boundless worlds be swiftly reborn in my land to enjoy happiness, and before long, may they all together attain the unsurpassed path.

May my diligence be ever steadfast and firm; May I constantly exercise a compassionate heart to uproot sentient beings, Delivering all those suffering in the Avīci hell, So that the great vows I have made shall never cease.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
“After the bhikṣu Dharmakāra had spoken these verses, he said to the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja:
‘I now resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; I joyfully seek supreme, perfect, and complete enlightenment.’”
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will describe the meritorious adornments of the buddha-fields.
If I may hear this, I shall constantly cultivate the practices for adorning a land.
At that time, the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja addressed the bhikṣu Dharmākara, saying:
"Reflect for yourself: what skillful means must you cultivate to be able to accomplish the adornment of a Buddha-field?
The bhikṣu replied, "My wisdom is shallow and limited;
I am unable to fully understand the practices for adorning a field."
“Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, we pray that you will proclaim for us the matters concerning the adornments of the buddha-fields.

Then, the Tathāgata Lokêśvararāja immediately proclaimed for them the vast, perfect, and magnificent characteristics of the meritorious adornments of eighty-four hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta buddha-fields, which could not be fully concluded even after the passing of one kalpa.
At that time, having heard these words, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
Regarding the length of the lifespan of that World-Sovereign King Buddha, why do you say that the land of that sutra endures for one kalpa?"
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"The lifespan of that Buddha will be a full forty kalpas, Ānanda!"

When that bhikṣu Dharmakāra heard the Buddha’s account of the meritorious adornments of eighty-four hundred thousand koṭis of nayutas of buddha-fields, he understood and mastered them all as clearly as if they were a single buddha-field.
Immediately, he prostrated himself at the Buddha’s feet within the assembly, took his leave, and withdrew.
He went to a secluded place and sat alone in contemplation, cultivating meritorious deeds to adorn a buddha-field, making great vows for the duration of five kalpas.
At that time, the bhikṣu Dharmakāra again went to the place of the Tathāgata Lokêśvararāja;

prostrating himself with his five limbs touching the ground, he paid homage at the feet of the World-Honored One. Having finished his prostration, he joined his palms and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
"In this way, I have now accomplished the meritorious adornments, practices, and vows of eighty-four hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta buddha-fields.
Then, the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
Your practice and vows have reached ultimate realization through contemplation; now is the very time for you to explain them for the sake of the assembly.
Upon hearing this Dharma, the bodhisattvas there will attain great and wholesome benefit, enabling them to cultivate the adornment of buddha-fields.
At that time, the bhikṣu Dharmakāra, having heard the Buddha’s holy command,
bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms toward the Buddha,
spoke to him: “World-Honored One!...”
I make this vow:
May I, like the World-Honored One, realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
and may the Buddha-field where I dwell be fully adorned with immeasurable and inconceivable merits.

All sentient beings, including those in the realm of Yama and within the three evil paths of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals, shall all be born in my land and receive my Dharma transformation; before long, they shall all attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and all shall obtain bodies of true golden color.
“World-Honored One!
Once I have attained Bodhi and become a Perfectly Enlightened One, may all sentient beings in the worlds of the ten directions be born in my land, just as they are in the lands of all Buddhas.”
The assembly of humans and devas, having distanced themselves from conceptual discrimination and attained tranquility of the faculties,
shall all be caused to realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“World-Honored One!...”

When I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings in the worlds of the ten directions be born in my land and attain great supernormal powers; within a single thought-moment, may they travel throughout hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddha-lands to make offerings to all Buddhas and deeply plant the roots of goodness, and may they all attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“‘World-Honored One!

Once I have attained bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings who are born in my land all obtain the supernormal power of recollecting past lives (*pūrvanivāsānusmṛti-jñāna*), such that they are able to skillfully observe events from hundreds of thousands of *koṭi-nayuta* kalpas in the past;
and may they all attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.’”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and become a Perfectly Awakened One, may all sentient beings who are born in my land all obtain the pure celestial eye, capable of seeing the coarse and subtle forms and signs of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of worlds;
and may they all attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings be born in my land; may they all attain the supernormal power of knowing the minds of others, skillfully understanding the mental states and mental factors of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings;
and may I cause them all to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings be born in my land; may they all abide in the stage of right faith, free from inverted perceptions and firmly cultivate their practice;
and may they all attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings be born in my land; may the roots of goodness from the right practices they cultivate be immeasurable, pervading the realm of quiescence without interruption;
and may they all attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings be born in my land; though they abide in the stages of Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, may they travel throughout hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of jewel-adorned lands to perform Buddha-works everywhere, and may I cause them all to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings be born in my land; may they all obtain boundless radiance capable of illuminating hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddha-fields;
and may they all attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and become a Perfectly Awakened One, may all sentient beings be born in my land, with their lives not cut short prematurely, and may they live for hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of kalpas;
may I cause them all to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings be born in my land so that no name of evil shall exist there. May they hear of immeasurable and innumerable Buddha-lands that are without names, without titles, without marks, and without forms, beyond all praise, yet without doubt or slander, their bodies and minds remaining unmoved;
may they all attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.”
“‘World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings who seek rebirth in my land, mindful of my name and giving rise to a sincere heart that is firm and non-regressive, be met by me at the time of their death with countless bhikṣus appearing before them in an encircling assembly. Within a mere moment, may they attain rebirth in my land;
and may I cause them all to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.’”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings throughout the infinite, boundless, and innumerable worlds of the ten directions who hear my name and resolve their minds upon Bodhi, planting various roots of goodness and seeking rebirth according to their wishes, be born in every Buddha-land without exception;
and may I cause them all to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
“World-Honored One!
Once I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings born in my land be endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man;
may they attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in a single lifetime.”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and become a Perfectly Awakened One, may all sentient beings be born in my land. If there are those with great vows who do not yet wish to attain Buddhahood but remain as Bodhisattvas, by my majestic power, I shall cause them to teach and transform all sentient beings, leading them all to give rise to faith and to cultivate the practices of Bodhi, Samantabhadra, quiescence, pure Brahma-conduct, and the most supreme conduct, as well as all wholesome deeds;
I shall cause them all to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings be born in my land, where they shall serve and make offerings to immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddhas in every place, planting various roots of goodness;
may their every aspiration be fulfilled according to their wishes, and may they all attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and become a Perfectly Awakened One, may all the bodhisattvas within my buddha-field achieve all-encompassing wisdom and be skilled in expounding the profound and secret meanings of all dharmas;
may they swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi before long.”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, all the bodhisattvas dwelling in my jewel-adorned land shall arouse a courageous mind and exercise great supernormal powers, traveling to the Buddha-lands throughout immeasurable, boundless, and innumerable worlds. There, they shall make offerings and serve with pearls, necklaces, jeweled canopies, banners and pennants, robes, bedding, food and drink, medicinal decoctions, fragrant flowers, and music, seeking thereby to attain bodhi;
may they swiftly achieve the realization of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
“‘World-Honored One!

When I have attained Bodhi and become a Perfectly Awakened One, may all the bodhisattvas dwelling in my Jewel Land who have resolved their minds on the Great Way and wish to serve and make offerings to the immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, of other worlds—with pearls, necklaces, jeweled canopies, banners and streamers, robes, bedding, food and drink, medicinal decoctions, fragrant flowers, and music—yet are unable to go there; at that time, by the power of my past vows, I shall cause those Buddhas, World-Honored Ones of the other worlds, each to extend their arms to reach into my land to receive these offerings, and cause them to swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.’”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and become a Perfectly Awakened One, may all the bodhisattvas dwelling in my jewel-adorned land, according to their own inclinations, never depart from this realm while desiring to make offerings to the infinite Buddhas of other directions with pearls, necklaces, jeweled canopies, banners and streamers, robes, bedding, food and drink, medicinal decoctions, fragrant flowers, and music.”
Furthermore, I reflected:
"If the Buddhas extend their arms to this place to receive offerings, it would be a weariness for the Buddhas that brings me no benefit.
While I was thinking this, by means of my supernormal power, I caused these offering articles to reach the presence of the Buddhas in other directions, making offerings to each one individually.
At that time, the Bodhisattva will before long fully realize Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
[He further said: "World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and become a Perfectly Awakened One, all the Bodhisattvas dwelling in my jewel-adorned land shall be sixteen yojanas in height, possess the strength of Nārāyaṇa, have physical forms that are upright and majestic with radiant light, and be fully endowed with roots of goodness."
"I shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
'World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and become a Perfectly Awakened One, all the bodhisattvas dwelling in my Jewel Land shall, for the sake of all sentient beings, penetrate the treasury of the Dharma, establish them in boundless universal wisdom, and exhaustively sever all fetters.'"
All shall attain and realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"World-Honored One!

Once I have attained *bodhi* and become a Perfectly Awakened One, all the bodhisattvas dwelling in my precious land shall fashion incense burners from hundreds of thousands of *koṭi-nayuta* varieties of rare jewels, extending from the surface of the earth up to the limits of space, constantly offering universal perfumes of priceless sandalwood to make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions."
"May they be enabled to swiftly attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
'World-Honored One!

Once I have attained *bodhi* and become a Perfectly Awakened One, the Buddha-field where I dwell shall be vast, magnificent, pure, and polished like a mirror, such that it can reflect all immeasurable and boundless Buddha-fields; and when sentient beings behold it, they shall give rise to a sense of rare wonder.'"
"Before long, he will swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
[He said: 'World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and become a Perfectly Awakened One, all the bodhisattvas dwelling in my Jewel Land shall constantly experience bliss day and night during the six periods, surpassing that of the devas; they shall enter the gate of the Samādhi of Universal Equality, and the radiance of their bodies shall universally illuminate boundless worlds.'"
Before long, he shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
[He further vows: "World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all women throughout the infinite, boundless, and innumerable worlds of the ten directions who feel weary of and seek to leave behind their female bodies, upon hearing my name, give rise to a pure mind, take refuge in me, and pay homage; at the end of that person's life, they shall immediately be reborn in my land and become male."
May they all attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
"World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and realized Perfect Enlightenment, may all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas in the infinite, boundless, and innumerable Buddha-fields of the ten directions who hear my name and practice the pure precepts become firm and non-regressive, swiftly sitting at the site of enlightenment;”
“I shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
‘World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and become a Perfectly Enlightened One, may all the Bodhisattvas in the infinite, boundless, inconceivable, and peerless Buddha-fields of the ten directions hear my name, prostrate themselves with their five limbs touching the ground, and take refuge in me. Furthermore, may all sentient beings among gods and humans respect, revere, draw near to, and serve me, thereby increasing their merit.’”
“I shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
‘World-Honored One!

Once I have attained *bodhi* and become a Perfectly Awakened One, may all sentient beings who give rise to pure faith, for the sake of śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas, dye robes, wash robes, cut robes, sew robes, and prepare monastic garments—whether making them with their own hands or employing others—and having done so, dedicate the merit;’”
By the merit they have inspired, for eighty-one lifetimes they shall obtain the finest garments, which shall follow them and provide them with abundance;
in their final body, they shall come to be born in my land and achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Adornment of Immeasurable Life, Spoken by the Buddha, Volume One.
The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Adornment of Immeasurable Life, Spoken by the Buddha, Volume Two.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Central India, Chao-san Dafu, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
The Dharma Master Facheng, Grand Master Mingjiao, translated by imperial decree:
"At that time, the bhikṣu Dharmakāra addressed the World-Honored One, saying:

'Once I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings who hear my name be forever freed from burning afflictions and attain a mind of cool serenity; may they practice right faith and be reborn in my land, where, sitting beneath jeweled trees, they shall realize the patience of non-arising.'"
“I shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
‘World-Honored One!

Once I have attained bodhi and become a perfectly awakened Buddha, may all the assemblies of Bodhisattvas in every Buddha-field throughout the ten directions, upon hearing my name, realize the samādhi of tranquility at that very moment.’”
Having dwelled in this samādhi, within a single thought-moment, one beholds immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, serving and making offerings to them,
and achieves *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and become a Perfectly Awakened One, may all the śrāvakas and bodhisattvas in all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, upon hearing my name, realize the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharmakṣānti*), accomplish all roots of goodness that are equal, and abide in effortlessness by being free from applied exertion;
and before long, may they cause them to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all the assemblies of Bodhisattvas in all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, upon hearing my name, give rise to a sense of wonder and immediately attain the Universal Bodhisattva Samādhi.”
Having dwelt in this samādhi, within a single thought-moment, one reaches immeasurable, innumerable, and inconceivable Buddha-fields, where one reveres, honors, and makes offerings to the Buddhas,
and achieves *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all the bodhisattvas within my land—whether they delight in preaching the Dharma, delight in listening to the Dharma, manifest supernatural powers, or travel to other regions—be able to practice as they wish and achieve complete fulfillment;
and may I cause them all to realize Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
“‘World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Bodhi and realized perfect enlightenment, may all those in every Buddha-field throughout the ten directions who hear my name immediately attain the first patience, the second patience, and even the patience of the non-arising of dharmas at that very moment;
and may they achieve Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.’”
At that time, after the bhikṣu Dharmakāra had made such a vow before that Buddha, by the Buddha’s majestic power, he spoke these verses:
“I now, in the presence of the Buddha, Make this sincere and truthful vow.”
He attained the body of the Buddha’s ten powers, with majesty and virtue beyond compare;
furthermore, he became a great king, wealthy and sovereign.
He extensively used all manner of treasures to bestow gifts universally upon the poor and suffering.
May those multitudes of living beings, throughout the long night, be free from sorrow and affliction;
may they give birth to manifold roots of goodness and achieve the fruit of Bodhi.
When I attain perfect enlightenment, I shall establish my name as Amitāyus.
Sentient beings who hear this name shall all come to my land;
possessing golden bodies like the Buddha’s, with all sublime marks perfectly complete,
they too shall, with a heart of great compassion, benefit all classes of living beings.
May the light of my wisdom shine far and wide upon the lands of the ten directions;
may it eliminate the darkness of greed, hatred, and afflictions within all sentient beings.
Those in the hells, the hungry ghosts, and the animal realm—may they all abandon the sufferings of the three miserable paths;
may they also be born within my land and cultivate pure conduct.
May I attain that body of radiant light, shining universally like the Buddha;
the brilliance of the sun, moon, and jewels cannot be compared to its radiance.
May I, in future ages, always act as a teacher of gods and humans.
Within billions of worlds, he utters the lion’s roar.
Just as those Buddhas of the past performed acts of compassion—
vast, immeasurable, and boundless— for billions of sentient beings, so too does he.
Fulfilling former vows, all shall attain Buddhahood.
When this great vow was made, the trichiliocosm shook throughout the ten directions,
and the devas and humans within the void of space [were moved].
A rain of all kinds of flowers, sandalwood, and aloeswood fell;
they praised the Great Bhikṣu, whose power of aspiration is most rare:
"He shall certainly become a Buddha and extensively benefit the realm of sentient beings."
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

At that time, after the bhikṣu Dharmakāra had made this vow before the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja, as well as the devas, humans, māras, brahmās, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, asuras, and others, he dwelt in true wisdom, applied himself with courageous diligence, cultivated immeasurable merit, adorned Buddha-fields, and entered samādhi."
Throughout great asaṃkhyeya kalpas, he cultivated the practices of a bodhisattva.
He gave rise neither to thoughts of stinginess and greed, nor thoughts of anger, nor thoughts of delusion;
nor did he have perceptions of desire, anger, or delusion, nor perceptions of forms, sounds, odors, tastes, or tangibles.

Their minds are not deluded or distracted; their speech is not mute; and their bodies are not indolent. They take delight only in recollecting the roots of goodness cultivated by the Buddhas of the past and practicing tranquil conduct; they remain far removed from falsehood and steadfastly maintain their moral discipline.
They constantly benefit sentient beings with kind speech, and they place deep faith, respect, and reverence in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, remaining disciplined, compliant, and gentle.
Relying on the gateway of ultimate truth, they plant the roots of all virtues and realize emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the unconditioned, non-arising, and non-ceasing.

He well guards his verbal karma by not disparaging the faults of others; he well guards his physical karma by not losing his moral discipline (*vinaya*); and he well guards his mental karma so that it is pure and untainted.

Regarding all kingdoms, cities, villages, male and female attendants, gold, silver, and precious jewels, as well as forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles—he is entirely without attachment to them.
He constantly benefits and brings joy to sentient beings through the practice of the six perfections—generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
His exemplary conduct is complete, and his roots of goodness are perfected.
In every place where they are born, immeasurable, countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of treasuries of precious jewels will emerge from the earth.
They will gather in and sustain immeasurable, countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Such practices are immeasurable and boundless, such that they cannot be fully described.
"Furthermore, Ānanda,
when the bhikṣu Dharmakāra was practicing the bodhisattva path, he honored and revered all Buddhas, serving and making offerings to them without ever ceasing."
As the kings of the Four Great Heavenly Kings, they constantly go to the Buddha’s dwelling to pay respectful homage, serve, and make offerings;
as the king of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, they constantly go to the Buddha’s dwelling to pay respectful homage, serve, and make offerings;

as the kings of the Yāma Heaven, Tuṣita Heaven, Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and Paranirmitavaśavartin Heaven, and even as the Great Brahmā King and others, they constantly go to the Buddha’s dwelling to pay respectful homage, serve, and make offerings.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

Residing in Jambudvīpa as a Wheel-Turning King (cakravartin), having received the consecration (abhiṣeka), together with his ministers, officials, and clansmen, he constantly goes to the Buddha’s dwelling to pay respect, prostrate, serve, and make offerings;
likewise, for the sake of kṣatriyas, brahmins, and others, he constantly goes to the Buddha’s dwelling to pay respect, prostrate, serve, and make offerings."

In this manner, throughout immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of kalpas, he drew near to various Buddhas and planted the roots of all virtues, thereby accumulating the realization of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

When the bhikṣu Dharmakāra was practicing the bodhisattva path, his mouth constantly emitted the fragrance of sandalwood, and all the pores of his body emitted the fragrance of utpala flowers; this fragrance universally perfumed immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable hundreds of thousands of nayutas of yojanas.
Any sentient beings who smelled this fragrance all gave rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"Furthermore, Ānanda,
when the bhikṣu Dharmakāra was practicing the bodhisattva path, his physical appearance was upright and majestic, fully endowed with the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics."

Furthermore, both arms were adorned with all manner of precious jewels, from which his hands constantly produced all kinds of clothing, food and drink, banners and pennants, parasols, musical instruments, and even all the most excellent necessities required by sentient beings, thereby benefiting and bringing joy to all beings and causing them to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, having heard the Buddha speak of the bodhisattva practice of the bhikṣu Dharmakāra, Ānanda addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"Is this bhikṣu Dharmakāra a buddha of the past?"
"Is he a future Buddha?
Or is he a present Buddha?
The World-Honored One replied:
"That Buddha-Tathāgata comes from nowhere when he comes, and goes nowhere when he goes;
he is without birth or extinction, and belongs neither to the past, the present, nor the future.
Yet, solely to fulfill his vows and deliver sentient beings, he currently resides in the Western Quarter."

A hundred thousand koṭis of nayutas of buddha-fields away from Jambudvīpa, there is a world named Sukhāvatī; the Buddha there is named Amitāyus, and it has been ten kalpas since he attained buddhahood.
There were immeasurable and innumerable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as well as an immeasurable and innumerable assembly of śrāvakas, who respectfully surrounded him as he preached the Dharma for them.
The light of that Buddha illuminated hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of immeasurable Buddha-fields in the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
likewise, it was so in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

That Buddha Amitāyus may manifest a transformed halo that extends for one yojana, two yojanas, three yojanas, or even for a hundred yojanas, a thousand yojanas, a hundred thousand yojanas, or a hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta yojanas, until it completely fills immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable buddha-fields."
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

This present radiance is named Immeasurable Light, Unobstructed Light, Constantly Shining Light, Non-empty Light, Beneficial Light, Light of Affection and Joy, Peaceful Light, Light of Liberation, Peerless Light, Inconceivable Light, Light that Surpasses the Sun and Moon, Light that Outshines All Worldly Radiance, and Stainless Pure Light. Such radiance universally illumines all worlds throughout the ten directions."

Devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, upon seeing this light, give rise to the bodhicitta for the sake of attaining benefit and happiness.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“Even if I were to remain for an eon to speak of the merits, benefits, and virtues of this radiance, I could not exhaust them.
Furthermore, Ānanda!”

The Tathāgata Amitāyus has such an assembly of immeasurable and innumerable śrāvakas—hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands, one koṭi, a hundred koṭis, a thousand koṭis, kaṅkara numbers, bimbara numbers, nayuta numbers, ayuta numbers, vivaha numbers, vatsara numbers, kharva numbers, asaṃkhyeya numbers, ten asaṃkhyeyas, a hundred asaṃkhyeyas, a thousand asaṃkhyeyas, a hundred-thousand asaṃkhyeyas, amaniya numbers, and inconceivable numbers—that they cannot be reached by any analogy or calculation.
“Ānanda! That Mahāmaudgalyāyana is foremost in supernormal powers; he can know the number of all boys and girls throughout the trichiliocosm in a single day and night.”

Suppose there were hundreds of thousands of koṭis of śrāvakas, each possessing supernatural powers equal to those of Mahāmaudgalyāyana; and suppose furthermore that each of these śrāvakas lived for hundreds of thousands of koṭi-nayutas of years, exhausting their entire lifespans to count those śrāvakas—this would not equal even one-hundredth part [of the merit].
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
It is like the great ocean, eighty-four thousand yojanas deep and vast without limit.

Suppose there were a person who took a single hair from their body, crushed it into a hundred koṭis of fine particles as minute as motes of dust, and cast each particle into the ocean and brought it out again; the volume of water remaining upon each particle would be exactly the same."
If one were to cast all these hairs and dust particles into it, what do you think:
would there be more water in the hair and dust,
or more water in the ocean?
Ānanda said to the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!
A hair-tip of water has not yet reached even half a cup, whereas the waters of the ocean are immeasurable."
The Buddha said, “Ānanda!

Among that assembly of śrāvakas such as Maudgalyāyana and the others, those who have calculated and known [the number of beings] throughout their entire lifespans are like the water on a hair-tip or a speck of dust; those who have not yet finished calculating are like the water in the great ocean.”
In this way, that Buddha has such immeasurable and incalculable numbers of śrāvaka disciples.
Furthermore, that buddha-field is immensely wealthy and vast, where beings experience only happiness and no suffering;
it is free from the retributions of the hells, hungry ghosts, animals, the realm of Yama, and the eight difficult conditions.
There were only pure bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and assemblies of śrāvakas.
"Furthermore, Ānanda,
in that buddha-field there are various jeweled pillars, all adorned with hundreds of thousands of rare treasures."

These were pillars of gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, pearl, musāragalva, and agate. Furthermore, there were pillars made of two precious substances—gold and silver; pillars of three precious substances—gold, silver, and lapis lazuli; pillars of four precious substances—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, and crystal; pillars of five precious substances—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, and pearl; pillars of six precious substances—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, pearl, and musāragalva; and pillars of seven precious substances—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, pearl, musāragalva, and agate.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

In that Buddha-land, there are also various kinds of jewel-trees, whose roots, trunks, branches, and limbs are formed of gold, while their flowers, leaves, and fruits are fashioned from white silver."
There are also jewel trees whose roots, trunks, and branches are made of white silver, while their flowers, leaves, and fruits are fashioned from lapis lazuli.
There are also jewel trees whose roots, trunks, and branches are made of lapis lazuli, while their flowers, leaves, and fruits are fashioned from crystal.
There are also jewel trees whose roots, trunks, branches, and leaves are composed of crystal, while their flowers, leaves, and fruits are manifested from pearls.
There are also jewel trees whose roots, trunks, and main branches are composed of pearls, while their flowers, leaves, and fruits are manifested from conch-shell.
There are also jewel trees whose roots, stems, and trunks are composed of mother-of-pearl, while their flowers, leaves, and fruits are transformed from agate.
There are also jewel trees whose roots, stems, and trunks are composed of agate, while their flowers, leaves, and fruits are transformed from gold.
There are also jewel trees, with roots of gold, trunks of silver, branches of lapis lazuli, tips of crystal, leaves of pearl, flowers of musaragalva, and fruits of agate.
There are also jewel trees, with roots of white silver, trunks of lapis lazuli, branches of crystal, tips of pearls, leaves of giant clam shell, flowers of agate, and fruits of gold.

There are also jewel trees, with lapis lazuli for their roots, crystal for their trunks, pearls for their branches, mother-of-pearl for their twigs, agate for their leaves, gold for their flowers, and silver for their fruits.
There are also jewel trees, with roots of crystal, trunks of pearls, branches of conch-shell, tips of agate, leaves of gold, flowers of silver, and fruits of lapis lazuli.
There are also jewel trees, with roots of pearl, trunks of conch-shell, branches of agate, tips of gold, leaves of silver, flowers of lapis lazuli, and fruits of crystal.
There are also precious trees, with roots of giant clam shell, trunks of agate, branches of gold, tips of silver, leaves of lapis lazuli, flowers of crystal, and fruits of pearl.

There are also jewel trees, with agate for their roots, gold for their trunks, silver for their branches, lapis lazuli for their twigs, crystal for their leaves, pearls for their flowers, and musaragalva for their fruits.
Such are the rows of trees made of the seven treasures in the world of Ultimate Bliss.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
That buddha-land is pure, adorned, vast, level, and even; it has no hills, ravines, pits, thorns, gravel, or mountains of earth and stone."
The Black Mountains, Snow Mountains, Jewel Mountains, Gold Mountains, Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountains, and the Great Iron Ring Mountains;
the ground consists solely of golden earth.
At that time, having heard these words, Ānanda addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
“The Four Great Kings and the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven dwell upon Mount Sumeru, the King of Mountains;
where will the Yāma Heaven and the others dwell?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"All the devas from the Yāma and Tuṣita heavens up to the realms of form and the formless realm dwell entirely in dependence upon the realm of space."
Ānanda said: "The realm of space is unimpeded; how can it serve as a basis for dwelling?
The retribution of the causes and effects of karma is inconceivable."
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"The retribution of your own body is inconceivable; the karmic retribution of sentient beings is inconceivable; and the holy power of all Buddhas is inconceivable."
Although that Buddha-land has no great oceans, there are springs and rivers flowing and intermingling everywhere;
their waters may be ten yojanas, twenty yojanas, thirty yojanas, or even up to hundreds of thousands of yojanas in width,
and twelve yojanas in depth.
The water is pure and endowed with the eight meritorious qualities;

it issues forth a subtle and wondrous sound, like the music of hundreds of thousands of varieties of instruments, which pervades all Buddha-fields. All sentient beings who hear it find delight and attain great happiness.
Furthermore, on both banks of the water, there are countless sandalwood trees and auspicious fruit trees, whose flowers are perpetually fragrant and whose radiance shines brilliantly.
When those sentient beings cross this water, they may require it to reach their feet, or their knees, or even up to their necks;
or they may require it to be cold, warm, swift-flowing, or slow-flowing.
Each of those waters accords with the inclinations of sentient beings, causing them to experience happiness.

Furthermore, from within the waters there emerge various sounds: the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Saṅgha, the sound of cessation, the sound of the absence of intrinsic nature, the sound of the perfections (*pāramitā*), the sound of the powers, the sound of fearlessness, the sound of thorough penetration, the sound of non-action, the sound of non-arising, the sound of non-extinction, the sound of tranquility, the sound of great loving-kindness, the sound of great compassion, the sound of joy and equanimity, and the sound of empowerment—such various subtle and wondrous sounds emerge.

Having heard this, sentient beings give rise to a pure mind, free from all discrimination, upright and impartial, maturing their roots of goodness, and never regressing from the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Furthermore, those born within that buddha-field do not hear the sounds of hell-beings, hungry ghosts, or animals; nor do they hear the sounds of yakṣas, of strife and contention, of harsh speech, of double-tongued speech, of killing, of stealing, or any other evil sounds.
Those sentient beings possess handsome and majestic physical forms, immeasurable merit and virtue, clear and lucid wisdom, and mastery over supernatural powers.

Their palaces, towers, pavilions, gardens, ponds, clothing, and bedding are like those of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Emanations (*paranirmita-vaśavartin*); they are fully provided with every means of supreme happiness.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

When the sentient beings of that land think of incense, flowers, and so forth, desiring to make offerings to the Buddhas, at the very moment they form this thought, flowers, incense, necklaces, ointments, powdered incense, banners, pennants, parasols, and various musical instruments arrive according to their wishes, filling the entire Buddha-field."

If one thinks of food and drink, medicinal decoctions, clothing, bedding, crowns, earrings, pearls, jeweled nets, and so forth, they will arrive as soon as they are recollected and pervade the entire Buddha-field.
Furthermore, when they further contemplate mani-jewels and other ornaments adorning palaces, towers, halls, and chambers— whether large or small, high or low—
at the moment of such contemplation, these appear before them according to their will, all fully and perfectly present.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

It is like a person who possesses little wealth and property; in the presence of a Kṣatriya king who has received the consecration of sovereignty, all that person's power and influence completely vanish."
Furthermore, all the majestic power of a kṣatriya is entirely eclipsed in the presence of Śakra, Lord of the Devas.
Moreover, all the majestic power of Śakra, Lord of the Devas, is entirely eclipsed in the presence of the gods of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations.

Furthermore, the majesty of all the Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas and others, as well as that of the Form and Formless Realms, does not manifest at all when compared to the Land of Utmost Bliss of the Tathāgata Amitāyus.
In this way, the adornments of merit in that land are inconceivable.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

In that Buddha-land, at every mealtime, fragrant winds arise spontaneously and blow upon the jewel trees; as the trees rub against one another, they produce subtle and wondrous sounds, proclaiming suffering, emptiness, impermanence, non-self, and the various pāramitās."
Furthermore, he blew so that the tree blossoms fell upon the ground, covering the entire buddha-field to a height of seven person-lengths; it was level, majestic, soft, and radiant.
When travelers came and went, treading upon the ground, their feet sank in to a depth of four finger-widths, as pleasant to the body as touching kāliṅga cloth.
After the mealtime had passed, these precious flowers sank into the ground and disappeared.
After a brief moment, a wind arose again, blowing the fallen flowers from the trees onto the surface of the ground, no different than before.
It is likewise during the first watch and the last watch of the night.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
In that Buddha-land there is no darkness, no stars, no sun or moon, no day or night, no grasping or rejecting, and no discrimination; it is purely uniform and without admixture."
They shall experience only pure and supreme bliss.
If there are sons or daughters of good family who have already been born [into this state] or who are yet to be born, these persons will certainly realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
What do you think?
Within that buddha-field, there are no three kinds of loss:
first, the mind is free from falsehood; second, there is no regression from one's station; and third, virtuous deeds are never in vain.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

To the east, there are worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, wherein the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, extend their broad and long tongues, emit immeasurable light, and speak words of truth, praising the inconceivable merits of the Buddha Amitāyus."

In the southern direction, there are likewise worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, wherein the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, extend their broad and long tongues, emit immeasurable light, and speak words of truth, extolling the inconceivable merit of the Buddha Amitāyus.

In the western direction, there are likewise worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, where the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, extend their broad and long tongues, emit immeasurable light, and speak words of truth, praising the inconceivable merit of Amitāyus Buddha.

In the northern direction, there are likewise worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, wherein all Buddhas, Tathāgatas, extend their broad and long tongues, radiate immeasurable light, and speak words of truth, extolling the inconceivable merit of the Buddha Amitāyus.

In this way, throughout worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the four intermediate directions, above, and below, all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, extend their broad and long tongues, emit immeasurable light, and speak words of truth, praising the inconceivable merit of the Buddha Amitāyus.
Ānanda! What do you think?
Do you wish for sentient beings to hear the name of that Buddha, to give rise to a pure mind, to remember and uphold it, to take refuge and make offerings, and to seek rebirth in that land?
When these people pass away, they shall all attain rebirth in the World of Ultimate Bliss and never regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If there are good men or good women who, upon hearing this sutra, accept and uphold it, read and recite it, copy it, and make offerings to it, continuing day and night without interruption, seeking rebirth in that land.

When this person approaches the end of life, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, together with his assembly of holy ones, will appear before them. In a mere moment, they shall attain rebirth in the World of Ultimate Bliss and never regress from their progress toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If there are sons or daughters of good family who, having already resolved upon Bodhicitta, maintain the various prohibitive precepts firmly without transgression, benefit sentient beings, and dedicate all roots of goodness they have performed toward them so that they may attain peace and happiness, while recollecting the Tathāgata Amitāyus of the West and his land."

When this person’s life comes to an end, they will possess the physical marks and various adornments of a Buddha; born within a jewel-adorned land surrounded by sages and saints, they will swiftly hear the Dharma and never regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If there are sons or daughters of good family who give rise to ten kinds of mental states, namely:

first, not stealing; second, not killing; third, not engaging in sexual misconduct; fourth, not speaking falsely; fifth, not engaging in frivolous speech; sixth, not using harsh words; seventh, not engaging in divisive speech; eighth, not being covetous; ninth, not being angry; and tenth, not being deluded."

Thus, throughout day and night, one should contemplate the World of Ultimate Bliss and the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, their manifold merits and manifold adornments, taking refuge with a sincere heart, prostrating, and making offerings.
When such a person approaches the end of life, they will be without alarm, without fear, and their mind will not be inverted; they shall immediately attain rebirth in that Buddha-land.

There are immeasurable and innumerable Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, who praise the merit and the name of the Buddha Amitāyus; having heard this Dharma, they shall never regress from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Adornment of Infinite Life Spoken by the Buddha, Middle Fascicle.
The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Adornment of Infinite Life Spoken by the Buddha, Lower Fascicle.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao-san Dafu, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
The Great Master Mingjiao, the Subject Faxian, translated by Imperial Decree:
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

In as many Buddha-fields in the eastern direction as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, within each and every field, there are immeasurable and innumerable Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, as well as immeasurable and innumerable assemblies of Śrāvakas, who use various fragrant flowers, banners, pennants, and precious canopies to make offerings to the Buddha Amitāyus of the Land of Utmost Bliss."

In Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River in the southern direction, within each and every field, there are likewise immeasurable and innumerable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and immeasurable and innumerable assemblies of śrāvakas, who offer various fragrant flowers, banners, pennants, and precious canopies to the Buddha Amitāyus of the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

In every single Buddha-field throughout worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the western direction, there are likewise immeasurable and innumerable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and immeasurable and innumerable assemblies of śrāvakas, who offer various fragrant flowers, banners, pennants, and precious canopies as offerings to the Buddha Amitāyus of the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

In Buddha-lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the northern direction, in each and every Buddha-land, there are likewise immeasurable and innumerable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as well as immeasurable and innumerable assemblies of śrāvakas, who offer incense, flowers, banners, pennants, and precious canopies to the Buddha Amitāyus of the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
"In the four intermediate directions, above, and below, it was likewise; each bowed at the Buddha’s feet and praised the meritorious adornments of the Buddha-land.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"In worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the eastern direction, Within each and every land, there are immeasurable [Buddhas]."
Bodhisattvas and śrāvakas, having generated the supreme resolve, each took fragrant flowers, jeweled canopies, and other offerings,
and carried them to the adorned buddha-field to make offerings to the Tathāgata Amitāyus;
having made these offerings, they prostrated at his feet and praised him as the most sublime and rare field of merit.
Likewise, in the western, southern, and northern directions, as well as the four intermediate points, above, and below— throughout worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—
the number of śrāvakas and bodhisattvas is the same;
they all extend their offerings with fragrant flowers.
Prostrating at his feet and circumambulating him with devotion, they further praised the Tathāgata’s profound past vows:
how he accumulated merit to universally adorn the immeasurable and boundless Land of Ultimate Bliss;
for though other Buddha-fields are magnificently adorned, none can compare to this precious realm of the Tathāgata.

Again, they offered celestial flowers to the Buddha; scattered in the void, the flowers formed a parasol canopy, spanning a hundred yojanas in length and breadth. Its colors and forms were magnificently adorned beyond compare;
it completely covered the Tathāgata’s precious land, as all beings congratulated one another and gave rise to joy.
In the past, throughout hundreds of thousands of kalpas, you accumulated immeasurable roots of goodness;
having cast off those bodies within the three realms of saṃsāra, you have now arrived at this pure land of liberation.
At that time, that Buddha Amitāyus, transforming and guiding the minds of bodhisattvas from other regions,
secretly employed his supernatural powers to manifest a great light. From the opening of his face,
thirty-six billion nayutas of rays issued forth, universally illuminating billions of thousands of buddha-fields.
Having thus universally illumined humans and devas, it immediately entered the uṣṇīṣa of the Tathāgata.
All sentient beings present in the assembly marveled at this unprecedented Buddha-light;
each and every one of them resolved to attain bodhicitta, vowing to transcend the toils of saṃsāra and reach the other shore.

At that time, when the World-Honored One had spoken these verses, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, who was present in the assembly, rose from his seat, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and spoke these words:
“World-Honored One!
By what causes and conditions does Amitāyus Buddha emit immeasurable light from his face to illuminate all Buddha-fields?

We pray that the World-Honored One will explain this through skillful means, so that all sentient beings and the bodhisattvas of other directions, having heard these words, may give rise to a sense of rare wonder, resolve their minds upon the Bodhi of the Buddha, and aspire to enter the stage of non-retrogression.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Listen attentively now!
I shall explain it for you."
That Buddha-Tathāgata, in the past, during immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas while he was a bodhisattva, made this great vow:

"When I attain perfect enlightenment in the future, if there are immeasurable sentient beings in the worlds of the ten directions who hear my name, or prostrate to and mindfully recollect it, or praise and take refuge in it, or offer incense, flowers, and other such offerings; [may they all attain liberation]."
Sentient beings who are thus swiftly born into my land shall attain liberation upon seeing this radiance.

If bodhisattvas see this radiance, they immediately receive a prediction of enlightenment and realize the stage of non-retrogression. Holding fragrant flowers and various offerings, they travel to the boundless pure lands throughout the ten directions to make offerings to the Buddhas and perform Buddha-work, thereby increasing their merit. After a mere moment, they return to their own land to enjoy all manner of bliss; for this reason, the radiance enters the crown of the Buddha’s head.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

As for the bodhi tree of the Buddha Amitāyus, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, it is one thousand six hundred yojanas in height; its branches and leaves extend eight hundred yojanas in all four directions, and its roots penetrate five hundred yojanas into the earth. Its flowers and fruits are in full bloom, displaying the colors of countless hundreds of thousands of precious jewels."

Upon those trees, they were further adorned with various ornaments such as moonlight mani-jewels, Śakra-maṇi jewels, wish-fulfilling maṇi jewels, ocean-holding maṇi jewels, great green gems, sahasrika jewels, necklaces of beloved gems, necklaces of great green gems, necklaces of red pearls, necklaces of blue pearls, and nets of gold and silver.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

Every morning at the hour of the dawn, a fragrant wind naturally arises and blows upon these jeweled trees; as the trees strike against one another, they produce subtle and wondrous sounds, the resonance of which is heard throughout immeasurable worlds."
Any sentient beings who hear it shall be free from ear diseases, until they achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
If there are sentient beings who see this tree, they shall not develop eye diseases during the interval until they attain Buddhahood.
If there are sentient beings who smell the fragrance of this tree, they shall not suffer from diseases of the nose until they attain Buddhahood;

nor shall they experience such ailments during that interval. If there are sentient beings who eat the fruits of this tree, their tongues shall likewise remain free from disease until they attain Buddhahood.
If there are sentient beings who are illuminated by the light of this tree, from that moment until they attain Buddhahood, their bodies shall remain free from illness throughout the interval.

If there are sentient beings who contemplate and visualize this tree, from that moment until they attain Buddhahood, their minds shall achieve purity, remaining far removed from the maladies of afflictions such as greed.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"In this way, the flowers, fruits, and trees of that buddha-field perform the work of a Buddha for all sentient beings; all of these are sustained by the great vows of that Buddha made in the past."
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas currently existing and those who will be born in that buddha-field in the future shall, in a single lifetime, attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

If there are bodhisattvas who, by virtue of their past vows, enter the realm of birth and death to roar the lion’s roar for the benefit of sentient beings, I shall cause them to perform buddha-works according to their wishes.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

In that buddha-field, all the bodhisattvas and śrāvakas possess physical forms that are upright and majestic, with radiant halos blazing intensely, illuminating hundreds of thousands of yojanas in every direction."
"There are two bodhisattvas whose bodily radiance shines afar across the trichiliocosm.
Ānanda addressed him, saying, "These two bodhisattvas possess such great bodily radiance; what are their names?"
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"As for these two bodhisattvas:
one is named Avalokiteśvara."
The second is named Mahāvīrya (Great Diligence).
He currently dwells in this world-system performing great benefit and happiness, and after his life ends, he shall be reborn in that land.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

All the bodhisattvas in that buddha-field have gentle and serene countenances, are fully endowed with the primary and secondary marks of excellence, have attained unimpeded mastery in meditative concentration and wisdom, and possess supernatural powers and majestic virtue that are entirely perfected.
Having entered deeply into the Dharma-gate, they attain the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharmakṣānti*) and reach ultimate clarity regarding the secret treasury of all Buddhas.
With their faculties subdued, their bodies and minds become supple, and they dwell peacefully in the quiescence of the Mahāyāna Nirvāṇa.
Deeply penetrating right wisdom, they are free from all residual habits and rely upon the noble path of the seven factors of enlightenment practiced by the Buddha.
They cultivate the five eyes to illuminate the ultimate truth and penetrate conventional reality; their eloquence, dhāraṇīs, and sovereign mastery are unimpeded;
and they skillfully understand the boundless expedient means of the world.
His speech is truthful and profound in its meaning; he delivers the True Dharma to deliver all sentient beings.

He views the three realms as equal, free from all conceptual discrimination—characterized by signlessness, unconditionedness, no cause, no fruit, no grasping, no relinquishing, no bondage, and no liberation. Having distanced himself from all inversions, he is firm and immovable like Mount Sumeru.
Wisdom is as clear as the sun and moon;
it is as vast as the ocean from which the jewels of merit emerge;
it is as blazing as fire that consumes the fuel of afflictions.
Patience is like the earth, being equal toward all;
it is like water, which is pure and washes away all dust and defilement; it is like space, which is boundless because it does not obstruct anything;
and it is like a lotus rising from the water, for it is free from all taints.
Like the roar of thunder, because it issues forth the sound of the Dharma;
like gathering clouds, because it brings down the rain of the Dharma;
like wind moving trees, because it causes the sprouts of bodhicitta to emerge.
It is like the cry of a bull-king, for it differs from that of other cattle;
it is like the majesty of a dragon-elephant, for it is difficult to fathom;
it is like the gait of a noble steed, for there is no failure in its course.
Like the lion’s posture, because he is free from fear;
like the nyagrodha tree, because his protective shade is vast;
like Mount Sumeru, because he is unmoved by the eight winds.
Like a vajra, for it shatters the mountains of heterodoxy;
like the body of Brahmā, for it gives birth to the assembly of Brahmās;
like a garuḍa, for it devours the poisonous dragons.
Like birds in the sky, they have no fixed dwelling;
like the contemplation of Maitreya, they are equal to the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*).

Thus, Bodhisattvas pervade the Buddha-fields, blowing the conch of Dharma, raising the banner of Dharma, beating the drum of Dharma, and lighting the lamp of Dharma; pure and free from faults, they are without delusion and without loss.

From their hands, they produced flower garlands, necklaces, ointments, powdered incense, and all manner of ritual offerings; carrying these, they went to hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddha-fields to make offerings to the Buddhas.

Furthermore, from his hands, he separately produced precious flowers which were scattered into the void; they transformed into precious canopies ten *yojanas* wide, or twenty *yojanas*, even up to hundreds of thousands of *yojanas*, pervading all Buddha-fields.
In a mere moment, they returned to their own lands; free from craving and attachment, without grasping or abandoning, their bodies and minds were tranquil.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"These bodhisattvas do not exist within the five turbidities of my land; even if one were to speak for hundreds of thousands of koṭis of kalpas, one could never exhaustively describe them."
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"All the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas currently in this land of mine have already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas and planted the roots of all virtues;
after their lives end, they shall all be reborn in the world of Ultimate Bliss."
"Ānanda! Arise, join your palms, and face west to pay homage.

At that moment, Ānanda immediately rose from his seat, joined his palms, and faced west. While he was prostrating himself, he suddenly beheld the Buddha of Infinite Life in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, his countenance vast and his physical marks majestic, like a mountain of golden hue.
Furthermore, I have heard that the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, of the worlds in the ten directions extol and praise the various merits of Amitāyus Buddha.
Ānanda said, "The pure land of that Buddha is unprecedented; I too wish and aspire to be born in that realm."
The World-Honored One replied:
"Those Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas born therein have already drawn near to immeasurable Buddhas and planted the roots of all virtues."
"If you wish to be born there, you should single-mindedly take refuge in and look up to him with devotion.
As he spoke these words, Amitāyus Buddha emitted immeasurable light from his palm, illuminating hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddha-fields in the eastern direction.

In this world, all the Black Mountains, Snow Mountains, Golden Mountains, Jewel Mountains, Mount Mucilinda, Mount Mahāmucilinda, Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountains, and the Great Iron Ring Mountains; as well as the great oceans, rivers, groves, trees, and the palaces of devas and humans—all these realms are clearly perceived without exception, just as when the sun rises it illuminates the world with its brilliance; so too is it here.

At that time, within the assembly—monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—all beheld the various adornments of the world of Sukhāvatī, as well as the Tathāgata Amitāyus surrounded and venerated by śrāvakas and bodhisattvas, like Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, rising from the great ocean.

At that time, the World of Ultimate Bliss, though situated beyond hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of lands to the west, appeared as if before one's very eyes through the Buddha’s spiritual power.

Furthermore, one sees that land as pure, level, and even, like the surface of the ocean, devoid of hills, precipitous mountains, grasses, trees, or any impurities; it is adorned solely with various jewels, where noble sages dwell together.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

Moreover, that Buddha of Immeasurable Life, together with his assembly of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas, shall likewise behold my body and the assembly of bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, humans, devas, and other beings in this Sahā world."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Maitreya, saying:
"Do you see the meritorious adornments of the world of Ultimate Bliss—the palaces, pavilions, gardens, terraces, flowing springs, and bathing pools?"
Maitreya!
Do you see the various devas of the desire realm, up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven of the form realm, raining down all kinds of fragrant flowers that fill the buddha-field and create its adornment?

Do you see that the assembly of Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas of pure conduct emits the voice of a Buddha to expound the sublime Dharma, such that it is heard throughout all Buddha-fields, bringing benefit and happiness to all?
"Do you see hundreds of thousands of koṭis of sentient beings dwelling in palaces within the void, moving along with their bodies?
Maitreya Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"Everything is seen exactly as the Buddha has described.
Maitreya addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Why is it that in this realm there is a class of sentient beings who, although they also cultivate wholesome deeds, do not seek rebirth?"
The Buddha told Maitreya:
"These sentient beings possess shallow wisdom; they cannot distinguish the western direction from the celestial realms, and for this reason, they neither delight in nor seek rebirth there."
Maitreya replied:
"These sentient beings engage in false conceptualization; if they do not seek a buddha-field, how can they escape saṃsāra?
The Buddha said:
“Maitreya! Is there any birth from a womb in the Land of Ultimate Bliss?
Maitreya replied:
"No, World-Honored One!
Those born therein are like the various devas of the desire realm, who dwell in palaces five hundred yojanas in height, sporting with sovereign ease; how could there be birth from a womb?"
“World-Honored One!
For what cause and by what condition do the sentient beings of this world dwell in the womb-birth?
The Buddha said:
“Maitreya! These sentient beings are unable to detach from signs regarding the roots of goodness they have planted; they do not seek the wisdom of the Buddha but give rise to false discrimination.
Because they are deeply attached to worldly pleasures and human rewards of merit, they are born from a womb.”

If there are sentient beings who, by means of signless wisdom, plant the roots of all virtues, purify their body and mind, remain far removed from conceptual discrimination, and seek birth in a pure land to advance toward the Bodhi of the Buddhas.
When such a person’s life ends, in a single instant they will sit upon a precious lotus flower in a Buddha’s pure land, their physical marks fully perfected.
How could there be birth from a womb? Maitreya!

You see those who are foolish and ignorant, who do not plant roots of goodness, but instead rely on worldly wisdom and clever eloquence to give rise to false discriminations that only increase their deviant minds; how can such people escape the great calamity of birth and death?

Furthermore, there are sentient beings who, although they plant roots of goodness, make offerings to the Triple Gem, and serve as great fields of merit, grasp at signs and engage in conceptual discrimination with such deep-seated emotional attachments that they are ultimately unable to escape saṃsāra.
The Buddha said to Maitreya:

"Suppose, for example, a Kṣatriya king who has received the consecration of his rank were to establish a great prison. Within that prison, he would install palaces, towers, balustrades, windows, and couches and seats, all adorned with rare jewels;
and as for the clothing and food required, nothing would be lacking or insufficient."

At that time, King Abhiṣikta banished the crown prince and confined him within a prison; he then provided him with money, treasures, fine silks, and bolts of cloth, allowing him to enjoy them as he pleased.
The Buddha said to Maitreya:
"What do you think?
Does that prince obtain happiness?"
Maitreya replied:
"No, World-Honored One!"

Although within that place there are halls, palaces, towers, pavilions, food, drink, clothing, money, silk, gold, and jewels to be enjoyed at will, their bodies are confined in a prison and their minds lack freedom; they seek only to escape.
The Buddha said to Maitreya:
"If the consecrated king does not abandon his transgression, could those ministers, elders, householders, and others cause the crown prince to be released from confinement?"
Maitreya replied,
“Since the king will not release him, how can he escape?
The Buddha said:
"So it is, so it is! Although those sentient beings cultivate merit and make offerings to the Triple Gem, they engage in false discrimination, seeking the fruits of human or celestial rebirth."

At the time of receiving this retribution, all that is required—the vessel-world in which they dwell, palaces, towers, clothing, bedding, food, drink, and medicinal decoctions—is entirely abundant; yet they are still unable to escape from the prison of the triple world, remaining constantly within saṃsāra without autonomy.

Even if parents, wives, children, or male and female relatives should wish to rescue and deliver one another, they will ultimately be unable to escape the king of karma of wrong views, nor can anyone abandon it.
"If all sentient beings sever false discrimination, plant the roots of all virtues without signs or attachments, they shall be born in a Buddha-field and forever attain liberation.
Maitreya Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

In this Sahā world and in all other Buddha-fields, how many bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have been born in the World of Ultimate Bliss, seen the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, and attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?
The Buddha said, “Maitreya!

In this Sahā world of mine, there are seventy-two koṭi-nayuta bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas and planted many roots of virtue; they shall be born in that land to personally attend upon and make offerings to Amitāyus Buddha, and there they will achieve anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
In the Buddha-field called Difficult to Endure, there are eighteen koṭi-nayutas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are born in that land."
In the buddha-field of Ratnagarbha, ninety koṭi-nayuta bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were born in that land.
In the buddha-field of Arciṣmat, twenty-two koṭi-nayuta bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were born in that land.
In the buddha-field of Amitābha, twenty-five koṭi-nayuta bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were born in that land.
In the buddha-field of Lokapradīpa, sixty koṭi-nayuta bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were born in that land.
In the buddha-field of Nāgārjuna, one thousand four hundred bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were born in that land.
In the buddha-field of Vimalaprabha, twenty-five koṭi-nayutas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were born in that land.
In the buddha-field of Siṃha, one thousand eight hundred bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were born in that land.
In the buddha-field of Śrīkūṭa, two thousand one hundred koṭi-nayuta bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were born in that land.
In the Buddha-field of Benevolent King, one thousand koṭi-nayuta bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were born in that land.
In the Buddha-field of Flower Banner, one koṭi bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were born in that land.
In the buddha-field of King of Radiance, twelve koṭis of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were born in that land.
In the buddha-field of Fearless One, sixty-nine koṭi-nayutas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were born in that land.
They shall all draw near to and make offerings to Amitāyus Buddha, and before long they will attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Buddha said, “Maitreya!
The adornments of merit of the Land of Ultimate Bliss are such that they could not be fully described even if one were to speak for immeasurable eons as numerous as those calculated.
If there are good men or good women who, upon hearing the name of Amitāyus Buddha, give rise to a single thought of faith and take refuge in him with veneration and worship;
"You should know that this person is not of the Lesser Vehicle (Hīnayāna), but is named the foremost disciple within my Dharma.
The Buddha told Maitreya:
