"If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, who copy, make offerings to, uphold, recite, or explain to others this sutra, and even for a single day and night contemplate the merits of that land and the Buddha’s body, such a person, at the end of life, will swiftly be reborn there and achieve Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"Furthermore, Maitreya!
This present sutra is profoundly deep and subtle, bringing vast benefit to sentient beings.
If there are sentient beings who receive, uphold, read, recite, transcribe, or make offerings to this True Dharma..."
When that person approaches the end of life, even if the great trichiliocosm were filled with raging fires, they would still be able to transcend them and be born in that land.
This person has already encountered past Buddhas and received the prediction of enlightenment; they are praised by all Tathāgatas, and unsurpassed bodhi will be accomplished according to their wish.
The Buddha said:
"Maitreya! A Buddha-world is difficult to encounter, and the True Dharma is difficult to hear; you should likewise practice in accordance with what the Tathāgata has practiced."
One shall provide great protection for this sutra for the long-term benefit of all sentient beings, ensuring that no beings fall into the hells adorned with the five destinies;
and one shall cause all sentient beings to plant and cultivate merit and goodness, seeking rebirth in pure lands.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"If one has not cultivated merit and wisdom in the past, One cannot hear this True Dharma;
Because you have already made offerings to all Tathāgatas, Therefore, you have heard this meaning."
Having heard this, one should uphold it, transcribe it, recite and chant it, explain and propagate it, and make offerings to it;
by thus seeking the pure land with a single-minded focus, one will certainly be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Even if a great fire should fill the three thousandfold world system, And those various adorned prisons;
That one can transcend all such calamities Is entirely due to the majestic power of the Tathāgata.
The merits by which that Buddha brings benefit and joy can only be known by a Buddha and a Buddha;
even if śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas filled the world, they could not fathom them, despite exhausting all their supernatural powers.
Even if long-lived sentient beings were to remain for countless koṭis of kalpas,
praising the Tathāgata’s body of merit, they would exhaust their entire lifespan without reaching the end of the praise.
The Dharma taught by the Great Sage, the Dharma King, benefits all living beings;
if there are those who receive, uphold, and revere it, the Buddha says such persons are true and virtuous friends.
At that time, when the World-Honored One spoke this Dharma, twelve koṭi-nayutas of people were distanced from dust and freed from defilement, attaining the pure Dharma-eye.
Eight hundred bhikṣus, their outflows exhausted and their minds liberated, attained liberation of mind.
Among the assembly of devas and humans, twenty-two koṭis of nayutas of beings realized the fruit of anāgāmin.
Furthermore, twenty-five *koṭis* of people attained the patience of the Dharma (*dharmakṣānti*) and became non-retrogressive.

Additionally, forty hundred-thousand *nayutas* of people gave rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, planted various roots of goodness, and all vowed to be reborn in the world of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*) to behold the Buddha of Immeasurable Life (*Amitāyus*).

Furthermore, in the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, there are those—whether currently living or yet to be born—who behold Amitāyus Buddha; numbering eighty thousand koṭis of nayutas each, they shall receive the prediction of Dīpaṃkara Buddha, being named the Tathāgata Mañjughoṣa, and shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
All those sentient beings, through the causal conditions of the past vows of Amitāyus Buddha, shall together attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
When the Buddha spoke these words, the trichiliocosm shook in six ways, and a rain of various fragrant flowers fell, accumulating up to the knees.
Furthermore, various devas in the void of space produced exquisite music, uttering sounds of sympathetic joy;
even the devas of the form realm all heard this and marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence.

At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, Maitreya Bodhisattva, and the entire great assembly, including the eight classes of devas, nāgas, and others, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Adornment of Infinite Life Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll II.
